## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Putta Sutta* (Iti 74; PTS It 62) is a short discourse in the *Itivuttaka* (section It 3.25) addressing the classification of children [SuttaCentral]. The Buddha delineates three types of sons and daughters in comparison to their parents: those of superior or heightened birth (*atijāta*), those of equal or similar birth (*anujāta*), and those of inferior or lowered birth (*avajāta*), defining these distinctions through ethical and spiritual behavior rather than caste or biological lineage [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records two full parallels in the Chinese Āgamas: *Zǐ* (子, T 765.126) and a discourse in the *Saṁyuktāgama* titled *Sānzhǒng zǐ* (三種子, SA 874) [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects extensive text reuse across 50 texts (759 matches), predominantly with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4, AN 5, AN 8, AN 3, AN 11, AN 10), the *Pāyāsi Sutta* (DN 23), the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), and the *Mātugāma Saṁyutta* (SN 37) [DharmaNexus].
